enumeration.method: Independent examination of every line beginning with the small-cap THEOREM heading across all 25 main-paper pages finds exactly Theorems 2.1-2.4 and 3.1-3.4. Heading labels, complete statement continuations and the separate-supplement notice were checked against rendered source pages.

checks: The independent inventory and final census pass separate validator calls. Every original theorem field is unchanged, and the inventory hash matches its prior source review.

Title, all three authors, arXiv v2 stamp of 27 March 2024, versioned source URL, 25-page count and PDF digest match the pinned source. Section 6 proofs are in the main paper; the page-23 supplement notice refers to a separate unopened document.

All eight full theorem statements were visually checked on pages 6,8,9,12,13,14,17. The three page-spanning statements retain their complete continuations, hypotheses, algorithms, constants, bounds and estimator quantifiers.

The full observation and mean/difference model, bounded Hölder convention and pointwise sub-Gaussian assumption were checked against pages 2,3,5,6. They do not impose smoothness on the subject curves or order alpha_delta above alpha_m.
The conventional restriction of P is recorded with both explicit n_s=0 passages. Its graph does not require source samples, the full transfer experiment or any of the named estimation algorithms.
Common and independent design reach is disjoint by theorem family. The generic algorithm chooses a design branch; its definition does not add both design assumptions to a theorem.

The minimax lower bounds quantify arbitrary estimators and have no local-polynomial, conventional, transfer or adaptive algorithm dependencies. Their neighboring upper-bound gap/density conditions are not silently inherited.

Algorithms 1-4 were visually checked on pages 7,8,11,17, retaining every step and the distinction between spacing-weighted and unweighted empirical validation loss. Both adaptive sections explicitly change the total target count to 2n_t.

Theorem 2.4 inherits the common upper-bound assumptions and R_C definitions; Theorem 3.4 inherits the independent assumptions and R_I definitions. Their empirical selection procedures replace the earlier oracle comparisons, and both repetition averages remain intact.

Twelve auxiliary passages resolve sizes, norm/asymptotic conventions, source averaging, inheritance, sample splitting and rate definitions. Eighteen source notes retain unresolved algorithm/domain conventions and printed inconsistencies without repairing source text.

Independent graph and selector checks cover all 14 interfaces, 36 direct uses and 68 deduplicated theorem connections. Every interface has source keywords, original passages, matching highlights and source-backed explanations for all related theorems.

source_notes: The inspected artifact is the pinned arXiv v2 preprint; equality with the final journal wording has not been established.
The entire PDF is the main paper. The separate supplement was not opened, and no appendix or supplement result was used to complete a statement or its dependencies.

Source-fidelity and dependency validation do not certify proof correctness or repair the printed algorithms. In particular, empty-interval selection, the free polynomial index, positive dyadic bandwidths and the duplicate threshold assignment remain documented.

The complete original class paragraph is retained for both its full and conventional applications. The latter is interpreted through the paper’s explicit no-source setup, with that projection limitation stated separately.

The source labels R_C and R_I are local scalar rate definitions inside their respective upper-bound Theorems. They are archived and resolved for adaptive reuse without inventing new statistical functionals.

unresolved_source_references.note: The main-text formulas call the noises independent and bound their uncentered absolute tails, but do not explicitly state zero means or independence between design points, curves and noises. A tail bound alone does not give mean-zero errors; these omissions can matter for identifying f^[t] from Y. The census does not supply extra assumptions or certify the rates under a repaired model.

The bounds hold for each given x with a common proxy, not for the supremum over x inside probability. Only subject/noise indices 1 and 11 are printed in the tail formulas. Subject copies are identically distributed, but identical noise laws are not stated explicitly in the observation prose. The original quantifier scope is preserved.

The prose suggests identical target and source counts, while the equations use distinct n_t,n_s,m_t,m_s. Subsequent formulas depend on their distinction. The exact equations control the recorded convention; no equalities across target and source are added.

The symbol P is introduced for the full transfer model and reused when n_s=0. The source does not separately formalize the projected law class. D17 preserves the original paragraph plus both no-source passages, and records its target-only application without importing source observations or transfer algorithms.

Omega(alpha) is the largest integer strictly below alpha. Algorithm 1 separately requires a positive integer degree, even where omega(alpha)=0. The degree constraints in both adaptive procedures still refer to unknown smoothness; a fixed known upper smoothness bound is not stated in these passages. Adaptivity is not strengthened beyond the source’s actual conditions.

M_delta first denotes a fixed supremum bound for a difference function, and later denotes a growing algorithm threshold log(n_t n_s). These roles are distinguished in the analysis while retaining the same source symbol. They are not equated as model parameters.

The source design endpoint is printed T_[m_t+1]^[s]=1 although the source gap maximum runs to m_s+1. The m_t index is retained in the original statement and inherited hypothesis archive; it is not changed to m_s.

The common bandwidths use slash notation such as ceil(m_t/2 B_t(d_t+1))^-1 without denominator parentheses. The literal typeset expressions are preserved rather than choosing a new operator grouping in the original statement.

The source requires a 1/m-packing and 1/(2m)-covering subcollection of arbitrary design points. Simultaneous existence is not established by the printed instruction, and it is not the standard maximal-packing radius pair. No replacement separation or coverage radius is substituted.

Uniform selection from each subject’s observations in each interval is undefined when that set is empty. This can occur for independent designs even under positive bounded densities, especially with the displayed small bandwidths. The later least-squares fallback does not define the preceding empty-set draw. No implicit skip rule is added.
The regression basis contains q-1 even though the interval index is r and q is not bound. Step 9 instead uses r-1. The free q is preserved and separately flagged.

The source does not specify interval endpoint assignment or a measurable tie-break among nonunique polynomial fits. It specifies zero when a solution is unavailable. Its set notation for pooled data also requires preserving multiplicities and distinct subject identities to represent K n_s subjects. These implementation conventions are recorded as unresolved, not inserted into source quotations.

The claimed max gap=o(1/m_t) is incompatible with m_t+1 nonnegative gaps summing to one. The theorem’s actual inherited bound is at most C_t/m_t. The weighted empirical loss itself sums only j=1,...,m_t and leaves the final endpoint gap out, as printed.

The estimator’s last source argument is D^[s,ell], while the experiment and rate use K source populations. Ell is not defined in this theorem. The original ell remains; the mismatch is not silently repaired.

The candidate sets use 2^r for positive r, incompatible with b in 1/Z+ required by the called base algorithm. The claimed literal inclusion of the theorem-optimal bandwidths also does not follow from a dyadic grid. Both source passages are retained.
Both assignments are to M_s: log n_s and log n_t n_s. M_delta is subsequently passed to A_TL but is not assigned by this step. The second M_s is preserved.

Theorem 3.2 requires B_t,B_delta at least Gamma_t and B_s at least Gamma_s, the upper density bounds. Algorithm 4 instead prints the lower bounds C_t,C_s. Moreover, its B constants do not appear in the candidate-grid formulas. No substitution is made.

Positive thresholds and negative powers of logarithms require suitable positive sample sizes, in particular n_t,n_s>1 where these choices are used. This fits eventual asymptotic use but is not a claim of well-definedness for every small integer sample size. Conventional n_s=0 formulas do not invoke the source-logarithm prescriptions.

ambient_resolution.shared: The target random-function experiment is D1 and the source experiment D2. Equation (4) in A1 resolves the balanced sample sizes and common design type. D3 is the bounded Hölder class, including the strict-integer function omega. D4 is the mean/difference restriction and D6 is the pointwise tail assumption; these are conditions on supplied functions/variables, with the observation interpretation fixed separately by P. D7 is the full transfer law class; D17 records the source-backed conventional target-only restriction. Common and independent designs are D8 and D9. A2 resolves functional norms, asymptotic constants and tilde notation. Standard ambient objects are expectation, probability, Lebesgue density/integration, iid sampling, finite sums, min/max, suprema/infima, argmin, ceilings, indicator functions, logarithms and positive integers. No appendix or separate supplement was used.
ambient_resolution.2.1: The target-only class D17 and sample D1 are explicit through n_s=0. D8 is restricted to the target grid. C_t, endpoints and max-gap bound are inline, as are the infimum over all target-data estimators and its risk formula. Alpha_m,L_m come from D4/D3; tau and fixed supremum bounds are in the model. The tilde rate and squared L2 norm are A2. No particular regression algorithm is required to state the all-estimator minimax result.
ambient_resolution.2.2: D7 supplies the transfer model and D8 the common design. The target/source gap inequalities, endpoints, all degree/bandwidth/threshold choices, the oracle selection rule and both R_C expressions are fully inline in the original theorem. D11 and D12 resolve the named candidate estimators and hence D10. Omega is D3. A5 and A6 preserve reusable hypothesis/rate passages for the adaptive theorem. The common source-endpoint index and slash notation remain literal.
ambient_resolution.2.3: The theorem ranges over arbitrary estimators based on target D1 and source D2 data, with full class D7 and common design D8. Its rate is inline. It does not require the particular upper-bound algorithm, the upper spacing bounds of Theorem 2.2, its logarithmic thresholds or oracle comparison. The mean/difference regularity is inherited through P, not through a proof reference.
ambient_resolution.2.4: The opening reference inherits the full common-design hypotheses and base-estimator specifications of Theorem 2.2, archived in A5. Algorithm A_ALC is D14, with target total 2n_t from A9 and the spacing-weighted empirical comparison. R_C is resolved by A6. The positive repetition count and averaging formula (5) are inline; repeated algorithm randomizations are not assumed to produce independent new data. The impossible little-o mesh remark A10 is not added as a theorem hypothesis.
ambient_resolution.3.1: Section 3.1 explicitly supplies n_s=0, so P is the target-only specialization D17. The design law eta_t comes from D9 and the statement explicitly adds absolute continuity and positive lower C_t/upper Gamma_t density bounds. The estimator quantifier is target-data only. Its rate is inline; neither source-density conditions nor a specific algorithm are needed. The statement’s concluding estimator clause continues onto page 13.
ambient_resolution.3.2: The model is D7 with the independent design D9, by A3’s explicit design replacement. The statement binds both two-sided density bounds, every bandwidth ceiling/cap, the constant degree conditions, thresholds, oracle choice and R_I formulas. D11,D12 resolve the named outputs and D3 resolves omega. A7/A8 archive the inherited specifications and rates. These choices differ from the common-design theorem and are not merged.
ambient_resolution.3.3: The full transfer class D7 and independent design D9 are imposed. The infimum is over arbitrary estimators of target and source data, not the proposed algorithm. The rate and all factors K are inline. The lower-bound statement does not explicitly assume the upper-bound density conditions. The last source index ell is preserved and unresolved rather than replaced by K.
ambient_resolution.3.4: The opening reference inherits Theorem 3.2’s hypotheses, archived in A7, while A_ALI is the distinct candidate-grid procedure D16. A9 supplies 2n_t total target subjects. The right-hand R_I quantities are defined in A8, and r_max plus the averaging formula (6) are inline. The source algorithm’s positive dyadic grid, duplicate M_s and density-constant mismatch remain documented. No common-design packing branch or weighted validation loss is imposed as an independent-design assumption.

review_limits: Main-paper source transcription and theorem-statement dependency review; no proof certification.
No separate supplement or appendix inspection.
